title.value: Fast and Furious Convergence: Stochastic Second-Order Methods under Interpolation
title.justification: The title accurately encapsulates the core focus of the paper, discussing the convergence properties of stochastic second-order methods implemented under interpolation conditions.
title.quote: Fast and Furious Convergence: Stochastic Second-Order Methods under Interpolation

analysis.description: The paper focuses on the performance of stochastic second-order optimization methods in machine learning, specifically under interpolation conditions. It investigates the Regularized Subsampled Newton method (R-SSN) and stochastic BFGS algorithms, analyzing their global linear convergence and local quadratic convergence capabilities in minimizing smooth and strongly-convex functions. The research includes empirical evaluations using both synthetic and real datasets for binary classification tasks, demonstrating the efficiency of these methods in terms of convergence speed and computational efficiency compared to first-order methods.

type.justification: The paper includes empirical evaluations of the proposed methods on various datasets, as evidenced by the experimentation and results sections, focusing on the implementation and effectiveness of the methods described.
type.quote: We empirically evaluate stochastic L-BFGS and a 'Hessian-free' implementation of R-SSN for binary classification on synthetic, linearly-separable datasets and real datasets under a kernel mapping.
